summary: Independent Forge cold read (./forge grill run --gate spec) of docs/specs/process-local-claude-continuity.md produced nine findings: resume-transcript accumulation vs. the retire-after-crossing ceiling, provider-id branching risk, process-local rows mutating lifecycle before being ignored, /compact lock/dedup ownership, failover handle carry-over, Claude SDK storage lifecycle vs. stable config/skills/credentials, deployment row-cleanup scope and stale-row reopen, read-model/status leakage on incomplete cleanup, and the decision-0158 ceiling / new-setting relationship. The amended spec resolves all nine as stated requirements; the human confirmed the two open design choices (per-runner ephemeral session-bearing SDK files; transactional Claude-only provider-session row/pointer deletion preserving DeepAgents rows). One closing AskUserQuestion round returned a clean frontier.
gaps: Cold read: the current design resumes the full Claude provider transcript and re-appends bounded briefings each runner, so overlapping briefing copies accumulate; the 150k ceiling is retire-after-observed-crossing, so a new runner can still reopen and reread a large transcript before retirement. Is cross-process provider continuity actually required, given Gantry already owns canonical continuity in Postgres?
Cold read: does core runtime decide this behaviour by branching on an Anthropic/Claude provider id? A provider-id branch is brittle and would not generalise to DeepAgents or future adapters.

Cold read: for a process-local adapter, could an existing active/ready/maintenance-compaction provider-session row still mutate lifecycle state, replay a compaction delta, affect /status, or set hasProviderResume before it is ignored?
Cold read: for /compact on a process-local adapter, who owns admission and deduplication, and is a provider-session lock required or created when no provider row exists?
Cold read: in a failover loop, could a Claude handle be carried into or persisted by the wrong attempt (e.g. a DeepAgents-to-Claude failover writing a Claude provider session)?

Cold read (confirmed choice 1): what is the lifecycle of Claude session-bearing SDK storage across runners, and does wiping it also remove stable non-session configuration, skills, and credentials that must remain materialized?

Cold read (confirmed choice 2): what exactly does deployment cleanup delete, and can incomplete cleanup leave stale Claude rows that a later runtime reopens or reports? Must DeepAgents rows be preserved?
Cold read: do public session-resume projections and /status exclude process-local provider-session rows even when cleanup was incomplete, or could they leak stale Claude rows?
contradictions: Cold read: the change appears to conflict with decision 0158's Claude-specific cross-process continuation and its context ceiling, and it is unclear whether a new runtime setting is introduced or whether limits.provider_session_max_input_tokens still applies to durable-resume adapters.
resolutions: Resolved in spec Why + Behaviour 1-3 and AC 1-2/4: Claude interactive lanes (worker and inline) start a fresh non-persistent SDK query (persistSession: false, no resume id, no persisted AgentInput.sessionId); a later runner rebuilds model-visible continuity from the bounded channel/thread snapshot plus the hydrated continuity block (recent scoped session digests, active durable memory, active jobs); runs/events stay canonical evidence but are not replayed. Cross-process provider continuity is dropped in favour of Postgres-owned canonical continuity.

Resolved in Behaviour 4 and AC 12: core runtime chooses behaviour from an adapter-owned provider-session continuity capability and never branches on an Anthropic/Claude provider id; Claude declares process-local continuity while DeepAgents keeps durable resume.

Resolved in Behaviour 5 and AC 3/11: the continuity capability is consulted before selecting or promoting a provider-session row; for process-local adapters active/ready/maintenance-compaction rows are ignored before they can mutate lifecycle, replay a delta, affect /status, set hasProviderResume, attach to runs, or raise context marks; read-model and /status exclude these rows even on incomplete cleanup.

Resolved in Behaviour 6 and AC 7: /compact selects the adapter strategy before any lock; for a process-local adapter the canonical durable session-compaction task is the admission/dedup owner, no provider-session lock is required or created, fresh-checkpoint behaviour captures the current canonical boundary best-effort and discards provider context, and concurrent commands return the existing already-running response.

Resolved in Behaviour 8 and AC 8: provider-session continuity belongs to the adapter for the active attempt; each attempt independently decides resume input and output persistence. Claude-to-DeepAgents failover may persist the successful DeepAgents checkpoint; DeepAgents-to-Claude failover must not carry or write a Claude provider session, and run/context marking identify the successful durable attempt only.

Resolved in Behaviour 9 and AC 9 (human-confirmed): Claude worker and inline session-bearing SDK storage is per-run and removed during normal runner cleanup, while stable non-session configuration, skills, and credentials remain materialized through their existing paths; legacy transcript/session directories are included in drained rollout cleanup.

Resolved in Behaviour 10 and AC 10 (human-confirmed): deployment transactionally deletes only Claude execution-provider session rows and clears their latest pointers while workers are stopped; DeepAgents rows survive; runtime independently ignores stale Claude rows so incomplete cleanup cannot reopen or report them; rollback starts fresh Claude contexts and never restores deleted transcripts.

Resolved in Behaviour 5 and AC 11: public session-resume projections and /status exclude process-local provider-session rows even when cleanup was incomplete; durable-resume adapters retain current reporting.

Resolved in Behaviour 11 and AC 12: no new runtime setting is introduced and limits.provider_session_max_input_tokens remains available for durable-resume adapters; a new accepted decision supersedes only decision 0158's Claude-specific cross-process continuation and rejected-alternative language while preserving its ceiling for durable-resume adapters.

citations.finding: core runtime must not branch on an Anthropic/Claude provider id; behaviour is adapter-capability driven
process-local rows ignored before promotion, delta replay, run attachment, status projection, and resume-state projection
/compact fresh-checkpoint strategy for process-local adapters with no provider-session lock
per-attempt adapter ownership of resume input/output in failover; DeepAgents-to-Claude must not carry a Claude handle
Claude session-bearing SDK storage is per-run/ephemeral while stable config, skills, and credentials remain materialized
drained rollout transactionally deletes only Claude provider-session rows/pointers; DeepAgents rows survive
no new runtime setting; ceiling preserved for durable-resume adapters; new decision supersedes only decision 0158's Claude-specific cross-process continuation

rounds.question: The amended spec resolves all nine Forge cold-read findings, and you've confirmed the two remaining design choices. Lock them in and close the spec grill: (1) Claude session-bearing SDK files are ephemeral per runner while stable config, skills, and credentials stay materialized; (2) drained rollout transactionally deletes only Claude provider-session rows and their pointers while DeepAgents rows survive. Any remaining gap before I record the spec-grill pass?
options: Confirm both — ephemeral SDK sessions + Claude-only row deletion (Recommended)
Ephemeral SDK sessions only; revisit deletion scope
rounds.chosen: Confirm both — ephemeral SDK sessions + Claude-only row deletion (Recommended)
